title: arXiv AI — 28 October 2026: top ten by visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This inferred ordering uses visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes among 38 candidate papers with a listed page from a 468-record pool; votes are platform-specific, not readership or downloads, and citation evidence for this very recent batch is limited.

sections.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
sections.abstract: PDRVLA learns compact physical-dynamics tokens from future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features to condition robot action generation without running a video world model online; the authors report strong results on four simulation benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 99.3% success on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv, attributing the results to physical-token prediction and supervision from a frozen video world model.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported main results are simulation-based; the authors identify object-centric geometry, contact states, and material properties as future predictive targets beyond the RGB, depth, and optical-flow features tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 146 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; four simulation-benchmark results reported by authors.

sections.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
sections.abstract: Hy-Nomas is an 8B diffusion video world model that supports free-form text commands and continuous camera control over multiple turns using cached history, structured captions, and action-aware causal attention.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report superior human-evaluation results over existing world models on multi-turn text interaction, camera control, interleaved control, and spatial-memory tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: Although Hy-Nomas leads on several interaction benchmarks, the authors report that it still trails Genie 3 in long-term spatial consistency; they identify robotic adaptation as requiring videos paired with robot actions and task-success evaluation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 114 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; authors report model weights, code, and benchmarks released.

sections.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
sections.abstract: The authors argue that effective bit budget, rather than feature-reconstruction error, better predicts downstream visual understanding and introduce Factorized Vector Quantization (FVQ) to sustain gains as the token budget grows.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that their industrial-scale FVQ model matches continuous representations on multimodal understanding and outperforms UniAR and Emu3-Chat by 22.8% and 59.2% on a nine-metric average, respectively.
sections.unique_caveat: The state-of-the-art claim is scoped to the reported comparisons and metrics; the authors also identify saturation in existing multi-codebook quantizers, which FVQ is designed to mitigate rather than a settled limit for all discrete representations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 91 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; linked project page and code/model resources.

sections.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
sections.abstract: ThinkWorld represents actions as discrete chains of world dynamics and uses predicted future states to learn action reasoning from robot demonstrations and unlabeled human videos.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report simulation and real-robot experiments showing human-to-robot transfer and generalization to unseen tasks and environments using shared Chain-of-Dynamics representations and reinforcement learning from imagined futures.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that training results use a single seed, so episode-level confidence intervals do not capture variation across independently trained checkpoints.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 52 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; author project page and OpenReview-hosted manuscript provide technical resources.

sections.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
sections.abstract: CodeCap-Bench tests executable code as a compact representation of video, using 323 videos across five structured-2D categories to measure caption faithfulness through question answering and reconstruction.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that code captions improve downstream reasoning accuracy and video-reconstruction fidelity over natural-language captions, while current models still miss complex temporal dynamics.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark is restricted to structured 2D content in five categories; the paper's results do not establish that code captions work as well for unrestricted natural video.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 50 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; author benchmark reports fine-grained annotations and a multi-level evaluation framework.

sections.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
sections.abstract: LociArt combines mask-conditioned local video stylization with a 100K-pair training set and benchmark for regional style quality, preservation of non-target regions, and temporal consistency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved regional style quality and spatial control with temporal consistency, and show qualitative multi-region editing despite training on single-region, single-style pairs.
sections.unique_caveat: Quantitative evaluation uses 80 source videos, 84 target masks, and 168 foreground/background cases; the more complex multi-region behavior is described qualitatively.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 44 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; linked project page and disclosed dataset/benchmark.

sections.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
sections.abstract: EvidenceConnect synthesizes visual questions that require connecting information across zoomed image regions, then uses the data for RLVR training of a model called Zooming without Zooming v2.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim that training on synthesized evidence-connection examples transfers to downstream benchmarks that were not used to tailor the synthetic data.
sections.unique_caveat: The data-generation pipeline filters examples using agreement among independent VLMs and region-ablation tests, so evaluation outcomes remain dependent on those model-based selection checks and the reported benchmark suite.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 28 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; abstract reports improvements across multiple perception and reasoning evaluations.

sections.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
sections.abstract: EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, images, audio, video, and mixed inputs into a shared embedding space and offers modality-selective loading, adjustable vision-token budgets, truncated dimensions, and quantized weights.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a Pareto frontier across multimodal embedding benchmarks, outperforming specialist models and models two to twelve times larger on their evaluation suite.
sections.unique_caveat: The performance claims are benchmark-bound and depend on the selected modality mix, encoder-loading choices, and embedding dimensions; deployment trade-offs are not established for every retrieval workload.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 26 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; model availability and multimodal benchmark claims are linked from the paper.

sections.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
sections.abstract: NLD-Uni transfers visual-understanding and image-generation capabilities into a unified discrete diffusion language model through cross-paradigm on-policy distillation and progressive self-refinement.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report state-of-the-art results among unified discrete diffusion LLMs across the listed understanding and generation tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The state-of-the-art claim is explicitly relative to unified discrete diffusion LLMs and the paper's evaluated tasks; it does not establish superiority over all autoregressive or continuous-diffusion systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 25 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; abstract reports multiple understanding and generation evaluations.

sections.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
sections.abstract: The authors show that top-k channel selection can avoid offline threshold calibration for routed-expert decoding and introduce a weight-derived reader that reduces expert reads while preserving most evaluated accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report retaining 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads and MoE-block speedups of 1.60–1.90× at batch one on their Triton kernels.
sections.unique_caveat: The results cover three post-trained MoE models and depend on the reported kernels and hardware; they do not establish the same speedups on other model architectures or serving stacks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 21 visible Hugging Face Papers upvotes at snapshot; linked code and measurements on three post-trained MoE models.
